questions.question: With the pointer edits held back until run B, how should BK-414 stand when this PR merges?

options.label: Keep open as [~] (Recommended)
options.description: BK-414 stays in BACKLOG.md marked [~]; the dossier gains a 'Pointers: pending run B' step. The item closes in the later pointer PR, which is also where the 30-day acceptance clock starts. No new ID.

options.label: Close, new ID for pointers
options.description: BK-414 moves to BACKLOG-DONE.md as [x] for the tool; a new BK item (next safe ID) holds the pointer edits and the acceptance re-walk. Two items, cleaner 'done' signal, one more ID to track.

questions.question: How should `backlog-find --spec <ID>` match the attribute line's comma-separated spec IDs (e.g. `BE-021, SQL-BLOB-012`)?

options.label: Exact ID, repeatable (Recommended)
options.description: `--spec BE-021` matches the token BE-021 only (not BE-0210), case-insensitive; `--spec` may be given several times and matches any. Covers the orient check: pass each spec ID the task touches.

options.label: Exact ID or family prefix
options.description: As above, plus `--spec BE-` (trailing dash) matches every BE-* clause. Wider orient sweep, one more rule to document and test.

Where should the pointer edits land so run B (from master) sees the tool?

options.label: Add to #1099 (Recommended)
options.description: One PR ships tool + pointers; BK-414 moves to BACKLOG-DONE.md as [x] in it and the 30-day acceptance clock starts at its merge. Run B starts after you merge #1099. #1099 grows by CLAUDE.md + skill edits, so it may warrant one more review round (I'd ask first).

options.label: Separate follow-up PR
options.description: #1099 merges as is (tool only, BK-414 [~]); a second small PR adds the pointers and closes BK-414. Two merges before run B can start, but each PR stays single-purpose.

questions.question: How wide should the pointers go?

options.label: CLAUDE.md + all lookup steps (Recommended)
options.description: One rule in CLAUDE.md § Backlog, plus the ~14 skill lines that fetch a single section or item (ship, pr, fix-pr, rvw-pr, orchestrate), each checked by hand. Every session, whatever skill it runs, gets the same instruction. Edit/close-out steps keep Read and Grep.

options.label: CLAUDE.md + run B's skills only
options.description: Rule plus only /ship, /pr, /fix-pr and /rvw-pr, the skills `/ship BUG-280` actually runs. Smaller diff; /orchestrate keeps its old wording until a later pass.

options.label: CLAUDE.md rule only
options.description: One rule, no skill edits. Smallest diff, but skill steps that name `CLAUDE-REFERENCE.md#anchor` will still read as 'go read the file', so run B may ignore the rule there.

questions.question: Run B will now differ from run A in two ways: the RFC interventions and the lookup tool. Record that in the run-B plan?

options.label: Add a note to run-b-plan.md (Recommended)
options.description: One line in `tmp/token-kit/run-b-plan.md` (main checkout, gitignored): run B includes the BK-414 tool and pointers, so a token difference from A is not attributable to the interventions alone. Lookups show as `hatch run backlog-*`/`ref-*` Bash calls in tokkit.

options.label: Leave the plan to me
options.description: I don't touch run-b-plan.md; you account for the confound yourself.
